A transition week is proposed for the last week of June, during which we would accept a delivery on the old day (as a courtesy to the supplier's existing route plan) and then switch to Friday starting 05/07/2024.

**4. IMPACT ANALYSIS**

4.1. **Receiving Operations:** Positive impact. Friday currently has no major vendor arrivals scheduled before noon. The receiving bay will be available and the full team (including the two clerks and the assistant manager who can be pulled from office duties on Fridays) can dedicate attention to the delivery. Estimated unloading time should drop from the current average of 2 hours 20 minutes to under 1 hour 30 minutes.

4.2. **Kitchen / Cold Storage:** Neutral to positive. The kitchen currently plans its weekly menu around the existing delivery day. Moving to Friday means the weekend menu will be based on goods received Friday morning, which is fresher than goods received mid-week and held until Saturday. The cold room has sufficient capacity for one additional day of storage; we have verified this with the engineering team.

4.3. **Supplier Logistics:** The supplier has confirmed capacity for Friday routing. Their dispatch schedule currently has a Friday run to the Lekki area that passes within 4 km of our Victoria Island outlet; adding our stop would be a minor detour. They have noted that Friday traffic on the Lekki-Epe expressway is heavier than mid-week after 15:00, but our delivery window is 07:00 – 11:00, which avoids the worst congestion.

4.4. **Cost Impact:** No direct cost increase. Fuel surcharge terms in the contract are based on distance, not day of week. Overtime costs for receiving staff are not expected to change, as the delivery remains within normal working hours.
**5. STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATION**

5.1. **Operations (internal):** The receiving supervisor, Mrs. Bello, was consulted on 28/05/2024. She confirmed that Friday is the quietest day for vendor arrivals and that the two permanent clerks plus the assistant manager can be reassigned without affecting the bank reconciliation that normally happens Friday afternoon. Her only concern was the 07:00 arrival time, as the security gate log shows the morning guard shift change happens at 06:45; she has agreed to have the bay door unlocked and the pallet jack staged by 06:50.

5.2. **Kitchen / Executive Chef:** Chef Amara was briefed on 29/05/2024. Her initial reaction was to note that the weekend menu relies on the Friday delivery for the Saturday brunch service. She requested that the delivery window be kept as early as possible so that the butcher can break down the protein order before the lunch prep begins at 10:00. The proposed 07:00 – 11:00 window satisfies this, and she has indicated she will adjust the weekly order sheet to be submitted by Thursday 16:00 instead of the current Wednesday 16:00 deadline. This internal deadline change does not affect the contract and will be handled by a separate memo to the kitchen staff.

5.3. **Supplier (FreshLink Foods Ltd.):** The supplier's operations manager, Mr. Adeyemi, was contacted by phone on 30/05/2024 and followed up by email. He confirmed the Friday routing capacity noted in section 4.3 above. He also raised the point that their dispatch system generates a proof-of-delivery (POD) document with the delivery day printed on it; if the change is approved, they will need at least two weeks' notice to reprogram the template and to update the standing route plan in their GPS units. The transition week described in section 3.4 provides this notice. Mr. Adeyemi further noted that their Friday run to Lekki typically carries a smaller load than the mid-week run, so our order volume (average 4.2 tonnes per delivery) will fit without requiring a second vehicle. He asked that we confirm the gate access procedure for Friday morning, as their usual Friday driver has not previously delivered to our Victoria Island outlet; we have forwarded the standard site access sheet.

5.4. **Finance / Accounts Payable:** The finance team was informed of the proposed change on 31/05/2024. They confirmed that the payment terms (net 30 days from date of invoice) are unaffected, as the invoice date will still be the delivery date. They noted that the delivery day change will shift the invoice receipt to Friday, which means the weekly payment run on Tuesday will capture the invoice in the same week; this is considered an improvement. No change to the purchase order numbering or the approval workflow is required.

5.5. **Procurement (internal):** The procurement officer, Mr. Okafor, reviewed the draft of this change request on 30/05/2024. He confirmed that the contract does not contain a "day of delivery" clause that would require a formal amendment rather than a change request; he verified that Clause 7.2 (Delivery Schedule) states only that delivery shall occur "on a weekly basis, on a day mutually agreed by both parties in writing." This change request serves as that written agreement once approved. Mr. Okafor also noted that the contract's force majeure clause (Clause 12) would still apply in the event that the supplier cannot make the Friday run due to road conditions or public holidays; he recommended that we attach a brief note to the approval file reminding the supplier of their obligation to notify us by Thursday 12:00 if the Friday delivery will be delayed.

5.6. **Alternative options considered:** During the consultation, three alternatives to the Friday delivery were discussed and rejected, as follows.

The Friday option was selected because it is the only one that meets the receiving team's availability, the kitchen's freshness requirement, the supplier's routing capacity, and the finance team's invoice timing without additional cost.

1. PRICE REVIEW – MAIN ITEMS

FreshLine opened with their new price list effective 1st Sept 2024. Compared to our current contract (which runs to 31st Aug), most staples are up modestly. Their justification: diesel for reefer trucks up 12% since June, and yam/plantain prices at Ikeja Central Market are volatile due to the rains.

Their proposed prices (per unit, Naira):

| Item | Current (Aug) | Proposed (Sept) | Change |
|------|--------------|-----------------|--------|
| Tomato, 50kg crate | 28,000 | 31,500 | +12.5% |
| Onion, 50kg bag | 22,000 | 24,000 | +9.1% |
| Fresh Pepper (rodo), 25kg | 19,500 | 21,000 | +7.7% |
| Irish Potato, 50kg bag | 25,500 | 26,500 | +3.9% |
| Carrot, 25kg bag | 14,000 | 15,000 | +7.1% |

| Green Beans, 15kg | 16,000 | 17,000 | +6.3% |
| Cucumber, 20kg | 12,000 | 12,800 | +6.7% |
| Plantain (unripe), bunch | 3,800 | 4,200 | +10.5% |
| Yam (white), 1 tuber | 2,400 | 2,700 | +12.5% |

I pushed back on tomato and yam. Tomato is our highest-volume item (we take 60–70 crates weekly across both kitchens). Mr. Obi said the 31,500 is their floor because the northern farms are still recovering from the flooding and most of what's coming to Ikeja is from the middle belt. He offered a "loyalty allowance" of 1,000 per crate if we commit to a minimum weekly volume (see section 2). That brings effective tomato price to 30,500. Still above current but more acceptable.

Yam: no movement. He said the tuber price is set by the market union, not FreshLine. I noted that for the record; we may need to look at alternative suppliers for yam or switch more menu items to rice/plantain in Q4. Chef Amara to advise.

2. VOLUME DISCOUNTS – NEW STRUCTURE

FreshLine proposed a new volume discount slab system, effective 1st Sept, replacing the old "5% if order above 200k" rule which was too vague.

Proposed slabs (weekly order value, before discount):

FreshLine Produce offers_credit_terms_days 30 days. Record status: current.

- 150,000 – 249,999: 2% discount
- 250,000 – 399,999: 3.5% discount
- 400,000 – 599,999: 5% discount
- 600,000 and above: 7% discount

Discount calculated on the total weekly invoice, applied at the end of the month as a credit note. No cash discount.

I asked how this interacts with the tomato loyalty allowance. Mr. Obi confirmed the tomato allowance is on top of the slab discount, but the tomato allowance only applies if we take at least 50 crates in that week. If we drop below 50 crates for two consecutive weeks, we lose the allowance for the following month.

Our current average weekly order is around 480k–520k (both kitchens combined). Under the proposed structure, that puts us in the 5% band. If Lekki branch ramps as planned (opening mid-Sept, soft launch), we should cross 600k by October, giving us 7%. I confirmed with Mr. Obi that Lekki orders count toward the same weekly total. He said yes, as long as the delivery address is within Lagos and the order is placed through the same account.

3. DELIVERY TERMS

Current arrangement: FreshLine delivers to Victoria Island kitchen (main) on Mon/Wed/Fri, and to the old Surulere kitchen on Tue/Thu. Delivery is free above 150k per drop; below that we pay 5,000 per trip.

Their proposal for the new structure (Sept onwards):

- Main VI kitchen: Mon, Wed, Fri (unchanged)
- Surulere: Tue, Thu (unchanged)
- Lekki (new): Tue, Thu, Sat – but Sat delivery attracts a 7,500 fee unless the order is above 200k for that drop alone.

I questioned the Sat fee. Mr. Obi explained that their drivers are on overtime on Saturdays and the market is busier so loading takes longer. I asked if we could shift Lekki to Mon/Wed/Fri to avoid the fee. Miss Funmi checked her sheet – she said Mon/Fri are already at capacity for their Lekki route, Wednesday has room. So we could do Lekki on Wed and Fri, but that leaves a gap between Fri and the next Wed. For a new kitchen with limited cold storage, that's not workable.

Alternative: keep Tue/Thu/Sat for Lekki and accept the Sat fee for now. I told them I'd raise this with management. Chef Amara is worried about the Sat fee being a recurring cost. We may also explore whether the fee can be waived if the Lekki order is part of the same weekly total that qualifies for the 7% slab – Mr. Obi said he'd take that back to his manager but wasn't optimistic.
Negotiation Note #NN-33 (contd.) — 20/08/2024

4. LEAD TIMES & ORDER WINDOWS

FreshLine Produce has_lead_time_days 1 days. Record status: current. This is their current controlled lead time, confirmed again with Miss Funmi this morning. She said it applies to all Lagos deliveries, including the new Lekki route, and has been in place since their warehouse moved to Oshodi in March. No change expected for Sept.

But the lead time is only for items they hold in stock. Special cuts and some imported greens (rocket, kale, the baby spinach we use for the salad bar) need 48 hours notice. I asked Miss Funmi to put together a list of what falls into the "special order" category so we can pin it to the kitchen noticeboard. She said she'd email it by Friday. Chef Amara has been caught out twice this month ordering kale with 24hr notice and getting a "not available" flag on the invoice. If the list doesn't arrive, I'll chase it Monday.

Order windows:

- Orders placed before 4pm are delivered next day (within the 1-day lead time).
- Orders placed after 4pm count as next-day orders but delivery slips to the day after that. This is a change from the old 6pm cutoff. Mr. Obi said the 4pm cutoff is because of the Oshodi traffic and their new dispatch system. I asked if we could get an exception for the VI kitchen since we're their oldest account. He said he'd check but not to hold my breath.
- Weekend orders: Sat delivery must be in by 2pm Friday. Sun delivery is not available at all. This was already the case but I want it recorded because the Lekki kitchen staff may not know.

I raised the question of whether the 1-day lead time is guaranteed during the week of a public holiday. Miss Funmi said no, and that holiday weeks go to 2 days. She pointed to the last line of the delivery schedule sheet which we've been ignoring. Noted.

5. PRICE REVISION MECHANISM (SEPT – DEC)

The slab discount structure from section 2 applies to the overall weekly total across all three kitchens. But there is a separate quarterly price review that hits in October. Mr. Obi mentioned it at the end of the meeting, almost as an afterthought:

- FreshLine reviews prices on the first Monday of Oct, Jan, Apr, Jul.
- The review is based on their cost index (fuel, market prices at Mile 12, and exchange rate for imported items).
- For us, the relevant question is whether the 5% / 7% slab discount is calculated before or after the price review. Mr. Obi wasn't sure. He said the discount is applied to the invoice total, and the invoice total is based on the reviewed prices. So if prices go up 8% in Oct, our 7% discount is on top of that. That's a real cost risk for us.

I asked if we could lock prices for Q4 given our volume commitment. Mr. Obi said no, the review is across all their customers, but he could offer a "volume protection" clause if we commit to 650k/week average for Oct–Dec. That would cap any single-item price increase at 5% for the quarter. I told him I'd take it to management. Chef Amara is keen because the Lekki ramp-up will push us over 600k anyway, so the protection may cost us nothing.

The protection clause is not yet agreed. Mr. Obi said he needs his manager's sign-off. He'll come back to us by Friday.

6. CREDIT TERMS – UPDATE ON THE 5-DAY SLIP

I told Chef Amara to brief the Lekki sous chef (Ngozi) on this. Ngozi has been approving invoices late at Surulere twice in the last month. If she does the same at Lekki, we could lose a delivery day. Chef Amara said she'd handle it directly.

7. PACKAGING & RETURNS (SMALL ITEM)

Not a big point but worth recording: FreshLine is moving to reusable crates for the Lekki route only, starting Sept. The crates are the same green ones they use for their other big customers. We need to return the crates within 48 hours of delivery, or we pay 250 per crate. The VI and Surulere kitchens will stay on the one-way cardboard boxes for now.

I asked for the crate count to be on the delivery note. Miss Funmi confirmed it will be.

documents.content:
2.1. The existing delivery day falls mid-week. This creates a bottleneck in our receiving bay because it coincides with the arrival of our primary beverage distributor and the weekly linen collection. On the current schedule, our receiving team is forced to split attention between three vendors within a four-hour window, resulting in extended turnaround times and occasional delays in getting goods to the cold room.

2.2. Staffing records for March, April, and May 2024 show that we have only two dedicated receiving clerks on duty during that window. The third receiving position has been vacant since February and is unlikely to be filled before July due to budget approval timelines. This is not a staffing complaint; it is a structural constraint that will persist regardless of hiring.

2.3. A shift to a different delivery day would allow us to stagger vendor arrivals. The beverage distributor and linen service are fixed to their current schedules by their own logistics contracts and cannot move. Our supplier under Contract #2024-001 has confirmed in writing (email dated 28/05/2024 from their dispatch coordinator, Mr. Femi Adeyemi) that they have capacity to adjust their truck routing to accommodate a new day without additional cost to us, provided the change is implemented with at least two weeks' notice.

2.4. We have also observed that the current delivery day occasionally falls on a public holiday or on days when the Third Mainland Bridge is subject to lane closures. In March 2024, one delivery was delayed by five hours due to an unannounced police checkpoint; the goods arrived at 16:40 instead of 09:30, and we had to reject a portion of the fish order due to temperature abuse. A different day of the week would not eliminate this risk entirely, but historical traffic data suggests the risk is lower on the proposed day.

**3. PROPOSED CHANGE**

3.1. It is requested that the weekly delivery day under Supply Contract #2024-001 be moved from its current mid-week slot to a new recurring day. The specific day requested is stated in Section 3.3 below.

3.2. The delivery window (07:00 – 11:00) and the minimum order quantity terms remain unchanged. No other clause of the contract is affected by this request.

3.3. **CR-118 requests new delivery day Friday. Record status: current.**

3.4. This change is intended to take effect from the first full week of July 2024, subject to approval. A transition week is proposed for the last week of June, during which we would accept a delivery on the old day (as a courtesy to the supplier's existing route plan) and then switch to Friday starting 05/07/2024.

**4. IMPACT ANALYSIS**

4.1. **Receiving Operations:** Positive impact. Friday currently has no major vendor arrivals scheduled before noon. The receiving bay will be available and the full team (including the two clerks and the assistant manager who can be pulled from office duties on Fridays) can dedicate attention to the delivery. Estimated unloading time should drop from the current average of 2 hours 20 minutes to under 1 hour 30 minutes.

4.2. **Kitchen / Cold Storage:** Neutral to positive. The kitchen currently plans its weekly menu around the existing delivery day. Moving to Friday means the weekend menu will be based on goods received Friday morning, which is fresher than goods received mid-week and held until Saturday. The cold room has sufficient capacity for one additional day of storage; we have verified this with the engineering team.

4.3. **Supplier Logistics:** The supplier has confirmed capacity for Friday routing. Their dispatch schedule currently has a Friday run to the Lekki area that passes within 4 km of our Victoria Island outlet; adding our stop would be a minor detour. They have noted that Friday traffic on the Lekki-Epe expressway is heavier than mid-week after 15:00, but our delivery window is 07:00 – 11:00, which avoids the worst congestion.

4.4. **Cost Impact:** No direct cost increase. Fuel surcharge terms in the contract are based on distance, not day of week. Overtime costs for receiving staff are not expected to change, as the delivery remains within normal working hours.

documents.title: Change Request #CR-118
documents.content:
**5. STAKEHOLDER CONSULTATION**

5.1. **Operations (internal):** The receiving supervisor, Mrs. Bello, was consulted on 28/05/2024. She confirmed that Friday is the quietest day for vendor arrivals and that the two permanent clerks plus the assistant manager can be reassigned without affecting the bank reconciliation that normally happens Friday afternoon. Her only concern was the 07:00 arrival time, as the security gate log shows the morning guard shift change happens at 06:45; she has agreed to have the bay door unlocked and the pallet jack staged by 06:50.

5.2. **Kitchen / Executive Chef:** Chef Amara was briefed on 29/05/2024. Her initial reaction was to note that the weekend menu relies on the Friday delivery for the Saturday brunch service. She requested that the delivery window be kept as early as possible so that the butcher can break down the protein order before the lunch prep begins at 10:00. The proposed 07:00 – 11:00 window satisfies this, and she has indicated she will adjust the weekly order sheet to be submitted by Thursday 16:00 instead of the current Wednesday 16:00 deadline. This internal deadline change does not affect the contract and will be handled by a separate memo to the kitchen staff.

5.3. **Supplier (FreshLink Foods Ltd.):** The supplier's operations manager, Mr. Adeyemi, was contacted by phone on 30/05/2024 and followed up by email. He confirmed the Friday routing capacity noted in section 4.3 above. He also raised the point that their dispatch system generates a proof-of-delivery (POD) document with the delivery day printed on it; if the change is approved, they will need at least two weeks' notice to reprogram the template and to update the standing route plan in their GPS units. The transition week described in section 3.4 provides this notice. Mr. Adeyemi further noted that their Friday run to Lekki typically carries a smaller load than the mid-week run, so our order volume (average 4.2 tonnes per delivery) will fit without requiring a second vehicle. He asked that we confirm the gate access procedure for Friday morning, as their usual Friday driver has not previously delivered to our Victoria Island outlet; we have forwarded the standard site access sheet.

5.4. **Finance / Accounts Payable:** The finance team was informed of the proposed change on 31/05/2024. They confirmed that the payment terms (net 30 days from date of invoice) are unaffected, as the invoice date will still be the delivery date. They noted that the delivery day change will shift the invoice receipt to Friday, which means the weekly payment run on Tuesday will capture the invoice in the same week; this is considered an improvement. No change to the purchase order numbering or the approval workflow is required.

5.5. **Procurement (internal):** The procurement officer, Mr. Okafor, reviewed the draft of this change request on 30/05/2024. He confirmed that the contract does not contain a "day of delivery" clause that would require a formal amendment rather than a change request; he verified that Clause 7.2 (Delivery Schedule) states only that delivery shall occur "on a weekly basis, on a day mutually agreed by both parties in writing." This change request serves as that written agreement once approved. Mr. Okafor also noted that the contract's force majeure clause (Clause 12) would still apply in the event that the supplier cannot make the Friday run due to road conditions or public holidays; he recommended that we attach a brief note to the approval file reminding the supplier of their obligation to notify us by Thursday 12:00 if the Friday delivery will be delayed.

5.6. **Alternative options considered:** During the consultation, three alternatives to the Friday delivery were discussed and rejected, as follows.

The Friday option was selected because it is the only one that meets the receiving team's availability, the kitchen's freshness requirement, the supplier's routing capacity, and the finance team's invoice timing without additional cost.

---------------------------------------------------------------------  
3. PROPOSED CHANGE  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
The HR Coordinator, in consultation with the Head of Kitchen Operations and the Finance Manager (Mr. Chidi Eze), proposes the following change:

3.1 Staffing ratio adjustment  
The staffing ratio used for scheduling front-of-house and kitchen staff in the two branches shall be revised to 0.75. This ratio is proposed as the current controlled value for the scheduling model and will replace the existing ratio in the workforce planning spreadsheet and the scheduling software (Sling).

The proposed ratio is to be applied as follows:
- For every 100 projected covers, the scheduling system will allocate 75 staff-hours across kitchen and service roles.
- The ratio will be used for both weekday and weekend schedules, with the Saturday brunch treated as a separate shift block using the same ratio.
- The ratio applies to the combined kitchen and service staff, not to each department separately.

3.2 Effective date  
If approved, the new ratio will take effect from Monday 17 March 2025. This date is chosen to allow the roster for the week of 10 March to be published as planned, and to give the HR team one full week to update the scheduling templates and notify the affected staff.

3.3 Scope  
The change applies to the Victoria Island outlet (VI) and the Lekki Phase 1 outlet (LK1). The Ikoyi outlet is not included in this request, as it operates under a different service model (private dining and events) and is not subject to the same volume fluctuations.

---------------------------------------------------------------------  
4. JUSTIFICATION  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
The proposed ratio is based on a time-motion observation conducted over five service days in February 2025. The observation team (two HR interns, supervised by the HR Coordinator) recorded the following average task times:

CR-129 requests staffing ratio 0.75. Record status: current.

- Plating and garnish: 1 min 45 sec per cover
- Expediting and quality check: 45 sec per cover
- Running to table: 1 min 10 sec per cover
- Handover to delivery rider: 2 min 30 sec per order (average order size 2.3 covers)

Summing these times and applying a 15% allowance for breaks, changeover, and unexpected delays yields an effective staff-hour requirement that is consistent with the proposed ratio. The calculation is shown in Annex B (Staffing Ratio Calculation, Rev 2).

The proposed ratio also accounts for the fact that the current vacancy in the junior cook cadre (two positions at VI, one at LK1) is not expected to be filled before the end of April 2025. Until then, the existing staff will need to cover the gap, and the revised ratio ensures that overtime hours are minimized while still maintaining service standards.

---------------------------------------------------------------------  
5. BUDGET AND COST IMPACT  
---------------------------------------------------------------------  
The financial impact of the proposed change has been assessed by the Finance Manager. The key figures are as follows:

- Additional staff-hours per week (combined across both outlets): approximately 84 hours.
- Weekly cost impact at the current average blended rate (including statutory deductions): approximately ₦385,000.
- Monthly impact: approximately ₦1,540,000.

This cost is partially offset by the reduction in overtime payments. In February 2025, the kitchen and service teams recorded 61 hours of overtime at the VI outlet and 44 hours at the LK1 outlet. Under the proposed ratio, the scheduled hours would absorb most of this overtime, reducing the overtime bill by an estimated 70%.

The net additional cost is therefore estimated at ₦620,000 per month, which is within the 2% contingency allowance set aside in the 2025 operations budget. No capital expenditure is required. The only software change is the update of the ratio parameter in Sling, which can be done by the HR Assistant without external vendor support.

documents.title: Negotiation Note #NN-33
documents.content:
---

1. PRICE REVIEW – MAIN ITEMS

FreshLine opened with their new price list effective 1st Sept 2024. Compared to our current contract (which runs to 31st Aug), most staples are up modestly. Their justification: diesel for reefer trucks up 12% since June, and yam/plantain prices at Ikeja Central Market are volatile due to the rains.

Their proposed prices (per unit, Naira):

| Item | Current (Aug) | Proposed (Sept) | Change |
|------|--------------|-----------------|--------|
| Tomato, 50kg crate | 28,000 | 31,500 | +12.5% |
| Onion, 50kg bag | 22,000 | 24,000 | +9.1% |
| Fresh Pepper (rodo), 25kg | 19,500 | 21,000 | +7.7% |
| Irish Potato, 50kg bag | 25,500 | 26,500 | +3.9% |
| Carrot, 25kg bag | 14,000 | 15,000 | +7.1% |
| Cabbage, 25kg bag | 9,500 | 10,000 | +5.3% |
| Green Beans, 15kg | 16,000 | 17,000 | +6.3% |
| Cucumber, 20kg | 12,000 | 12,800 | +6.7% |
| Plantain (unripe), bunch | 3,800 | 4,200 | +10.5% |
| Yam (white), 1 tuber | 2,400 | 2,700 | +12.5% |

I pushed back on tomato and yam. Tomato is our highest-volume item (we take 60–70 crates weekly across both kitchens). Mr. Obi said the 31,500 is their floor because the northern farms are still recovering from the flooding and most of what's coming to Ikeja is from the middle belt. He offered a "loyalty allowance" of 1,000 per crate if we commit to a minimum weekly volume (see section 2). That brings effective tomato price to 30,500. Still above current but more acceptable.

Yam: no movement. He said the tuber price is set by the market union, not FreshLine. I noted that for the record; we may need to look at alternative suppliers for yam or switch more menu items to rice/plantain in Q4. Chef Amara to advise.

2. VOLUME DISCOUNTS – NEW STRUCTURE

FreshLine proposed a new volume discount slab system, effective 1st Sept, replacing the old "5% if order above 200k" rule which was too vague.

Proposed slabs (weekly order value, before discount):

FreshLine Produce offers_credit_terms_days 30 days. Record status: current.

- 150,000 – 249,999: 2% discount
- 250,000 – 399,999: 3.5% discount
- 400,000 – 599,999: 5% discount
- 600,000 and above: 7% discount

Discount calculated on the total weekly invoice, applied at the end of the month as a credit note. No cash discount.

I asked how this interacts with the tomato loyalty allowance. Mr. Obi confirmed the tomato allowance is on top of the slab discount, but the tomato allowance only applies if we take at least 50 crates in that week. If we drop below 50 crates for two consecutive weeks, we lose the allowance for the following month.

Our current average weekly order is around 480k–520k (both kitchens combined). Under the proposed structure, that puts us in the 5% band. If Lekki branch ramps as planned (opening mid-Sept, soft launch), we should cross 600k by October, giving us 7%. I confirmed with Mr. Obi that Lekki orders count toward the same weekly total. He said yes, as long as the delivery address is within Lagos and the order is placed through the same account.

3. DELIVERY TERMS

Current arrangement: FreshLine delivers to Victoria Island kitchen (main) on Mon/Wed/Fri, and to the old Surulere kitchen on Tue/Thu. Delivery is free above 150k per drop; below that we pay 5,000 per trip.

Their proposal for the new structure (Sept onwards):

- Main VI kitchen: Mon, Wed, Fri (unchanged)
- Surulere: Tue, Thu (unchanged)
- Lekki (new): Tue, Thu, Sat – but Sat delivery attracts a 7,500 fee unless the order is above 200k for that drop alone.

I questioned the Sat fee. Mr. Obi explained that their drivers are on overtime on Saturdays and the market is busier so loading takes longer. I asked if we could shift Lekki to Mon/Wed/Fri to avoid the fee. Miss Funmi checked her sheet – she said Mon/Fri are already at capacity for their Lekki route, Wednesday has room. So we could do Lekki on Wed and Fri, but that leaves a gap between Fri and the next Wed. For a new kitchen with limited cold storage, that's not workable.

Alternative: keep Tue/Thu/Sat for Lekki and accept the Sat fee for now. I told them I'd raise this with management. Chef Amara is worried about the Sat fee being a recurring cost. We may also explore whether the fee can be waived if the Lekki order is part of the same weekly total that qualifies for the 7% slab – Mr. Obi said he'd take that back to his manager but wasn't optimistic.

documents.title: Negotiation Note #NN-33
documents.content:
Negotiation Note #NN-33 (contd.) — 20/08/2024

4. LEAD TIMES & ORDER WINDOWS

FreshLine Produce has_lead_time_days 1 days. Record status: current. This is their current controlled lead time, confirmed again with Miss Funmi this morning. She said it applies to all Lagos deliveries, including the new Lekki route, and has been in place since their warehouse moved to Oshodi in March. No change expected for Sept.

But the lead time is only for items they hold in stock. Special cuts and some imported greens (rocket, kale, the baby spinach we use for the salad bar) need 48 hours notice. I asked Miss Funmi to put together a list of what falls into the "special order" category so we can pin it to the kitchen noticeboard. She said she'd email it by Friday. Chef Amara has been caught out twice this month ordering kale with 24hr notice and getting a "not available" flag on the invoice. If the list doesn't arrive, I'll chase it Monday.

Order windows:

- Orders placed before 4pm are delivered next day (within the 1-day lead time).
- Orders placed after 4pm count as next-day orders but delivery slips to the day after that. This is a change from the old 6pm cutoff. Mr. Obi said the 4pm cutoff is because of the Oshodi traffic and their new dispatch system. I asked if we could get an exception for the VI kitchen since we're their oldest account. He said he'd check but not to hold my breath.
- Weekend orders: Sat delivery must be in by 2pm Friday. Sun delivery is not available at all. This was already the case but I want it recorded because the Lekki kitchen staff may not know.

I raised the question of whether the 1-day lead time is guaranteed during the week of a public holiday. Miss Funmi said no, and that holiday weeks go to 2 days. She pointed to the last line of the delivery schedule sheet which we've been ignoring. Noted.

5. PRICE REVISION MECHANISM (SEPT – DEC)

The slab discount structure from section 2 applies to the overall weekly total across all three kitchens. But there is a separate quarterly price review that hits in October. Mr. Obi mentioned it at the end of the meeting, almost as an afterthought:

- FreshLine reviews prices on the first Monday of Oct, Jan, Apr, Jul.
- The review is based on their cost index (fuel, market prices at Mile 12, and exchange rate for imported items).
- For us, the relevant question is whether the 5% / 7% slab discount is calculated before or after the price review. Mr. Obi wasn't sure. He said the discount is applied to the invoice total, and the invoice total is based on the reviewed prices. So if prices go up 8% in Oct, our 7% discount is on top of that.
